instructions: Screen the standalone if in candidate.text, which is its containing sentence. If the sentence has multiple if occurrences, only the one enclosed in <target>...</target> is selected; those tags are program-added location markers, not source content. You see the sentence and its role, not the rest of the conversation. Decide whether this occurrence could express a condition affecting a specific matter. rule means a candidate conditional relationship, NOT a confirmed user-adopted rule. A later model reads the full conversation to confirm adoption and resolve references. Use unclear when a plausible relationship needs missing context to resolve pronouns, scope, or adoption; do not reject it just because the speaker is an assistant or refers to that/it. Preserve possible consequences and changes without a specified replacement. Reject clear non-rules: if meaning WHETHER, courtesy offers, ordinary preference-based suggestions, generic explanations with no candidate specific dependency, and actual requests to forget or withdraw a rule. An assistant policy proposal or quoted conditional relationship whose adoption is unknown is unclear, not automatically not_rule. Judge only the selected occurrence when the sentence has several if clauses. Do not invent context. This is a conservative screen: retain unclear if adoption, negation, quotation, referents or conditional context requires the full conversation. Exclude only clearly unrelated uses.

criteria.rule: The sentence expresses a candidate condition-to-consequence relationship for a specific matter; forward for confirmation.
criteria.not_rule: This occurrence is clearly not a candidate conditional rule under state.rule_policy.
criteria.unclear: A possible conditional relationship needs context to resolve its references, scope or adoption; forward for confirmation.
